sources_considered.why: Read the abstract and version history of primary research on thematic concentration.
Read the findings and explicit causal limitations of the same research.
Primary research on the compute divide offers a related causal mechanism, but measures institutions rather than alternative ideas.
read_page returned HTTP 403; the underlying research was read instead.

evidence_items.publisher: arXiv; Joel Klinger, Juan Mateos-Garcia and Konstantinos Stathoulopoulos
evidence_items.locator: Discussion, paragraph on mechanisms shaping the field
evidence_items.explanation: The study finds stagnating thematic diversity and a narrower private-sector research focus in data extending into 2020. Its discussion explicitly says the descriptive analysis does not establish the causal impact of private-sector participation.

evidence_items.publisher: arXiv; Nur Ahmed and Muntasir Wahed
evidence_items.explanation: The paper reports evidence that deep learning and unequal compute access changed institutional participation in AI research. Displacement of institutions does not by itself establish displacement of numerous alternative research approaches.

unresolved_gaps: The thematic-diversity study is descriptive and expressly leaves causal mechanisms untested.
The compute-divide study measures institutional participation, not the resources lost by alternative approaches.
No sufficiently broad records linking specific alternative approaches' lost support to Big Data prioritization were located.
